chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'And when they are taken in marriage' (fa-idha uhsinna). He said: 'Their being taken in marriage (ih-san) is that they are copulated with.' I said, 'If they have not been copulated with, is there no Penalty (Hadd) on them?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.إِحْصَان: Marriage consummation / being taken in marriage
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: The Words of Allah the Exalted

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of marriage consummation for slaves and when does the Hadd penalty apply?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that 'ih-san' for female slaves refers specifically to consummation (sexual intercourse), distinguishing it from the mere act of taking possession. It establishes that the Hadd penalty for fornication applies to them even before consummation, highlighting the unique legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence where they are subject to fixed penalties but with distinct conditions compared to free women.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj the High [4:25] and when they are taken in marriage. Heasws said: ‘Their being married is that they have been copulated with’. I said, ‘If he has not copulated with them, is there no Penalty (Hadd) on them?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes (there is)’.
